study type: retrospective nationwide cohort study and a nested case-control study
exposure: systemic disease (including preeclampsia, eclampsia, HELLP syndrome)
outcome: intracerebral hemorrhage during pregnancy or puerperium (pICH)
significant disability (modified Rankin Scale = 3-5) 3 months after pICH
cohort: Women with incident intracerebral hemorrhage during pregnancy or puerperium (pICH) and three matched controls with a pregnancy without ICH were identified in Finland from 1987-2016.
finding: Hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (HDP) were identified as the most important risk factor for intracerebral hemorrhage during pregnancy or puerperium (pICH), which carried a high maternal mortality rate of 12.5% and significant disability in 20.9% of survivors.
